items.name: Gnoll Alpha
items.description: Every pack has its top dog. Bigger, maybe. Often, though, with these lank and filthy mutts, it's not about size or sharp teeth but about cruelty—a willingness to kill your brothers and eat them while the pack watches.

items.name: Orc Bloodwarrior
items.description: The orcish horde is a savage, bloodthirsty, and hateful collection of tribes. Every able orc, be it man or woman, child or elder, swears fealty to the warchief and their tribe and bears the jagged blade of a bloodwarrior. Men are trained to fight and kill—orcs are born to it.

items.name: Orc Berserker
items.description: Stained in the unholy ritual of Anointing By The Night's Blood, some warriors of the horde rise to a kind of twisted knighthood, trading their sanity for this honor. The rare berserker that lives more than a few years becomes horrible and twisted, growing horns or an extra arm with which to grasp the iron cleavers they favor in battle.

items.name: Orc Breaker
items.description: Built more like an ogre or a troll, an orc breaker wields a hammer bigger than any man ought to be able to lift. They can't make plate of their own, so maybe it's jealousy that drives these burly things to crush and shatter the armored knights of the civilized lands.

items.name: Orc One-Eye
items.description: In the name of He of Riven Sight and by the First Sacrifice of Elf-Flesh do we invoke the Old Powers. By the Second Sacrifice, I make my claim to what is mine—the dark magic of Night. I call to the runes! I call to the clouded sky!
moves: Make a sacrifice and grow in power

items.name: Orc Shaman
items.description: The orcs are as old a race as any. They cast bones in the dirt and called to the gods in the trees and stone as the elves built their first cities. They summon the powers of the world to work, to fight and to protect their people, as they have since the first nights.

items.name: Orc Slaver
items.description: Red sails fly in the southern sea—the warfleet of the horde. Orcs down that way have taken to the sea, harassing island towns and stealing away with fishermen and their kin, especially if they can get their hands on elves.

items.name: Orc Shadowhunter
items.description: Not every attack by orcs is torches and screaming and enslavement. Among those who follow He of Riven Sight, poison and murder-in-the-dark are considered sacred arts. Do not be so distracted by the howling of the berserkers that you don't notice the knife at your back.

items.name: Orc Warchief
items.description: There are chiefs and there are leaders of the tribes among the orcs. There is but one Warchief. One orc in all the horde who stands above the rest, bearing the blessings of the One-Eyes and the Shamans both, bearing the Iron Sword of Ages and carrying the ancient grudge against the civil races on his shoulders.

items.name: Triton Spy
items.description: A fishing village caught one in their net, some time ago. Part a man and part some scaly sea creature, it spoke in a broken, spy-learned form of the common tongue before it suffocated in the open air, telling of a coming tide and a triton empire that would rise up and drag the land down into the ocean.
items.instinct: To spy on the surface world

items.name: Triton Tidecaller
items.description: Part priest, part outcast among their kind, the tidecaller speaks with the voice of the deeps, known by their mutations—transparent skin, rows of teeth like a shark, glowing eyes or fingertips. They ride wild hippocampi and cast strange spells that rot through the wooden decks of ships.
moves: Cast a spell of water and destruction

items.name: Triton Sub-Mariner
items.description: The triton are not a militant race by nature, but this trend begins to change as the tidecallers come to rally their people. Sub-mariners swim in formation, wielding pikes and harpoons and attack the crews of ships that wander too far from port.

items.name: Triton Noble
items.description: The triton ruling houses were chosen, they say, at the dawn of time, granted lordship over all the races of the sea by some now-forgotten god. In ages past, they were known for their sagacity, but the tidecallers' prophecy is changing that: nobles are expected to be strong, not wise.

items.name: Angel
items.attack: Sword of Flames (b[2d10]+4 damage, ignores armor)
items.description: So was it written that the heavens opened up to Avra'hal and did an angel from the clouds emerge to speak unto her. 'Be not afraid,' it commanded her. 'Go to the villages I have shown you in your dreams and unto them show the word I have written on your soul.' The word the angel wrote upon the soul of Avra'hal was 'kill'.

items.name: Barbed Devil
items.description: There are a thousand forms of devil, maybe more. The barbed devil appears only at a site of great violence or when called by a wayward summoner. Covered in sharp quills, this particular demon revels in the spilling of blood, preferably by impaling victims piecemeal or in whole upon its thorns.
items.instinct: To rend flesh and spill blood

items.name: Chain Devil
items.description: Do you think the phrase 'drag him to hell' means nothing? It is unfortunately literal, in the case of the chain devil. Appearing differently to each victim, this summoned creature has but a single purpose: to wrap its victim up in binding coils and take it away to a place of torment.

items.name: Concept Elemental
items.description: The planes are not as literal as our world. Clothed in the elemental chaos are places of stranger stuff than air and water—rivers of time crash upon shores of crystal fear. Sometimes, the spirits of these places can be lured into our world, though they are infinitely more unpredictable and strange than mere fire or earth might be.
moves: Demonstrate its concept in its purest form

items.name: Corrupter
items.description: Surely, my good man, you must know why I am here. I've come to give you what you've always wanted, friend. Glory, love, money? Paltry things when you've the vaults of hell to plumb. You have but one thing we desire. Promise it to us, and the world shall be yours for the taking. Trust me.
moves: Offer a deal with horrible consequences
Plumb the vaults of hell for a bargaining chip

items.name: Djinn
items.description: Stop rubbing that lamp, you idiot. It will not grant you wishes. The djinn once dwelt in the true city of Majilis, made of brass by the spirits, with golem servants and human lovers. The djinn still sometimes come to these places, and they are powerful and wicked and proud.
moves: Summon the forces of the City of Brass

items.name: Hell Hound
items.description: When one reneges on a deal, does not the debtor come for payment? So too with the Powers Below. They only want what is theirs. A howling pack of shadows, flame and jagged bone, driven by the hunting horn. They will not cease, they cannot be evaded.
moves: Summon the forces of hell on their target

items.name: Imp
items.description: These tiny observer-demons often act as a first-time binding subject by neophyte warlocks. They can be found infesting arcane cabals, drinking potions when no one watches, and chasing pets and servants with tiny pitchforks. A caricature of true demonhood.

items.name: Inevitable
items.description: All things come to an end. Reality bleeds from the cut of entropy's knife. At the edge of time itself stand the inevitable. Massive, powerful and seemingly carved from star-stuff themselves, the inevitable intervene only where magic or calamity have undone the skein of fate, guiding things back to the proper order.
moves: Enforce a law of nature or man

items.name: Larvae
items.description: Those who have seen visions of the Planes Below, and survived with their sanity intact, speak of masses of these writhing wretches. Maggots with the faces of men and women, crying out for salvation in a nest of flames. Once here, they spread misery and sickness during their mayfly lives before expiring into a slurry of gore.

items.name: Nightmare
items.description: The herd came from a pact made in the days when folk still inhabited the Blasted Steppes. One of theirs, in a bid to dominate his peers, made a black pact with some fell power and traded away his finest horses. Now the fiends of the pit ride on the finest horses ever seen: coats of shining oil and manes of tormented flame.
moves: Sheath a rider in hellish flame

items.name: Quasit
items.description: An imp with some ambition. A quasit is a kind of foot soldier in the demon realm. Commonly bound by warlocks to carry heavy loads or build bridges or guard their twisted towers, a quasit can take on many forms, none of them pleasant.

items.name: The Tarrasque
items.description: Legendary unstoppable juggernaut—eater of cities and swallower of ships, horses, and knights. It cannot be killed. No blade can pierce its stony shell nor spell penetrate the shield it somehow bears. It slumbers, somewhere in the periphery of the planar edge, for now.
moves: Swallow a person, group, or place whole
Release a remnant of a long-eaten place from its gullet

items.name: Word Demon
items.description: All of mortal magic is just words. Word daemons are called by accident, appear at random and are often short-lived, but come to attend a particular word. Capricious, unpredictable and dangerous, yes—but possibly useful, depending on the word.
moves: Cast a spell related to their word

items.name: Bakunawa
items.description: Dragon-Turtle's sister is a mighty serpent queen. Ten yards of scales and muscle, they say she wakes with a hunger when the sun disappears from the sky. She is attracted by bright light in the darkness and, like any snake, sneaky. Give the greedy snake your treasures and she might just leave you alone.
moves: Lure prey with lies and illusions

items.name: Basilisk
items.description: Few have seen a basilisk and lived to tell the tale. Even without its ability to turn your flesh to stone with a gaze, it is a dangerous creature. A bit like a frog, bulbous eyes and six muscled legs built for leaping. A bit like an alligator, with snapping jaws and sawing teeth. Covered in stony scales and very hard to kill.
moves: Turn flesh to stone with a gaze
Retreat into a maze of stone

items.name: Black Pudding
items.description: How do you kill a pile of goo? A great, squishy pile of goo that also happens to want to dissolve you and slurp you up? That is a good question to which I have no answer.
moves: Eat away metal, flesh, or wood
Ooze into a troubling place: food, armor, stomach

items.name: Coutal
items.description: As if in direct defiance of the decay and filth of the world, the gods granted us the coutal—a serpent in flight on jeweled wings, glowing with a soft light. Bright, wise, and calm, a coutal often knows many things and sees many more. They seek to cleanse and to purge and to make of this dark world a better one.
moves: Pass judgment on a person or place
Offer information in exchange for service

items.name: Crocodilian
items.description: It's a really, really big crocodile. Seriously. So big.
moves: Hold something tight in its jaws

items.name: Doppelgänger
items.description: Their natural form, if you ever see it, is hideous—like a creature who stopped growing part-way, before it decided it was elf or man or dwarf. Without form, without shape to call their own, maybe all they really seek is a place to fit in. If you go out into the world, when you come back home, make sure your friends are who you think they are.
moves: Assume the shape of a person whose flesh it's tasted

items.name: Dragon Turtle
items.description: Bakunawa has a brother. Where she is quick to anger and hungry for gold, he is slow and sturdy. A great turtle that lies in the muck and mire for ages as they pass, mud piled upon his back—sometimes trees and shrubs, sometimes a whole misguided clan of goblins building their huts on his shell.
moves: Bring its full bulk to bear

items.name: Dragon Whelp
items.description: Did you think they were all a mile long? A dragon whelp can still belch up a hellish ball of fire that'll melt your armor shut and drop you screaming into the mud. Their scales are softer than those of their bigger kin, but can still turn aside an arrow or sword not perfectly aimed.
moves: Start a lair, form a base of power

items.name: Ekek
items.description: Ugly, wrinkled bird-folk. Once, maybe, in some ancient past, they were a race of angelic men from on high, but now they eat rats that they fish from the murk with talon-feet and devour with needle-teeth. They understand the tongues of men and dwarves but speak in little more than gibbering tongues.
moves: Carry out the bidding of a more powerful creature

items.name: Fire Eels
items.description: These strange creatures are no bigger or smarter than their mundane kin, but have an oily secretion that oozes from their skin, and with a twist of their body they can ignite the stuff, leaving pools of burning oil atop the surface of the water and roasting prey and predator alike.
moves: Catch someone or something on fire (even underwater)

items.name: Frogman
items.description: Croak croak croak. Little warty munchkins. They stand as men, dress in scavenged cloth and hold court in their froggy villages, speaking a rumbling pidgin form of the tongue of man and constantly at war with their neighbors. Greedy and stupid but clever enough when they need to defend themselves.

items.name: Hydra
special_qualities: Only killed by a blow to the heart
items.description: A bit like a dragon, wingless though it may be. Heads, nine in number at birth, spring from a muscled trunk and weave a sinuous pattern in the air. Cut off a head and two more grow in its place. Only a strike, true and strong, to the heart can end a hydra's life.
moves: Regenerate a body part (especially a head)

items.name: Kobold
items.description: The kobolds are beholden slaves to dragons and were, in ancient times, their lorekeepers and sorcerer-servants. Their clans, with names like Ironscale and Whitewing, form around a dragon master and live to serve and do its bidding. Spotting a kobold means more are near—and a mighty dragon cannot be far, either.
moves: Call on dragons or draconic allies

items.name: Lizardman
items.description: A traveling sorcerer once told me that lizardmen came before we did—that before elves and dwarves and men built even the first of their wattle huts, a race of proud lizard kings strode the land. Now they dwell in places men long forgot or abandoned, crafting tools from volcano-glass and lashing against the works of the civilized world.

items.name: Medusa
items.description: The medusa are children of a serpent-haired mother, birthing them in ancient times to bear her name across the ages. They dwell near places of civilization, luring folks to their caves with promises of beauty or riches untold, curating strange collections of their victims frozen forever in stone.
moves: Turn a body part to stone with a look

items.name: Sahuagin
items.description: The shape and craft of men wedded to the hunger and the endless teeth of a shark. Voracious and filled only with hate, these creatures will not stop until all life has been consumed. They are hunger and bloodlust, driven up from the depths of the sea to ravage coastal towns.
moves: Frenzy at the sight of blood

items.name: Sauropod
items.description: Great lumbering beasts, they live in places long since forgotten by the thinking races of the world. Gentle if unprovoked, but mighty if their ire is raised, they trample smaller creatures with the care we might give to crushing an ant beneath our boots.

items.name: Swamp Shambler
items.description: Some elementals are conjured up in sacred circles etched in chalk—a sort of science to it. Others aren't so orderly; some are a natural confluence of vine and mire and fungus. They do not think the way a man might think. They simply are. Spirits of the swamp. Shamblers in the mud.
moves: Call on the swamp itself for aid

items.name: Troll
items.description: Tall. Real tall. Covered all over in warty, tough skin. Big teeth, stringy hair like swamp moss and long, dirty nails. Near impossible to kill, unless you've fire or acid to spare—cut a limb off and watch: in a few days, you've got two trolls where you once had one.
moves: Undo the effects of an attack (unless caused by a weakness, your call)

items.name: Will-o-wisp
items.description: Spot a lantern floating in the darkness, lost traveler in the swamp. Hope—a beacon of shimmering light. You call out to it, but there's no answer. It begins to fade and so you follow, sloshing through the muck, hoping you're being led to safety. Such a sad tale that always ends in doom.
moves: Clear a path to the worst place possible

items.name: Abomination
special_qualities: Many limbs, heads, and so on
items.description: Corpses sewn onto corpses make up the bulk of these shambling masses of dark magic. Most undead are crafted to be controlled, but not so the abomination—the ritual used to grant fire to their hellish limbs invokes a hatred so severe that it knows but one task: to tear and rend at the very thing it cannot have—life.

items.name: Banshee
items.description: Come away from an encounter with one of these vengeful spirits merely deaf and count yourself lucky. A victim of betrayal, the banshee makes known her displeasure with a roar or scream that can putrefy flesh and rend the senses. If you can help her get her vengeance, they say she might grant rewards.
moves: Drown out all other sound with a ceaseless scream

items.name: Devourer
items.description: When a particularly wicked person dies in a gruesome way, the dark powers of Dungeon World might bring them back to a kind of life. The devourer does not feed on the flesh of men or elves—the devourer eats souls, drawing breath like a drowning man and swallowing a soul at the moment of a victim's expiry.

items.name: Dragonbone
items.description: Mystical sorcerers debate: is this creature truly undead or is it a golem made of a particularly rare and blasphemous material? The bones, sinews and scales of a dead dragon make up this bleak automaton. It would take a being of some considerable evil to twist the remains of a dragon thus.

items.name: Draugr
items.description: In the Nordemark, the men and women tell tales of a mead hall atop their heavenly mountain where men of valor go after death. Those who fall to poison or in an act of cowardice aren't welcome there. Some come back, frozen and twisted and empowered by jealous rage, and wage their eternal war on the towns of the men they once knew.

items.name: Ghost
items.description: Every culture tells the story the same way: you live, you love or you hate, you die somehow you're not too fond of, and here you are, ghostly and full of disappointment. Some brave and kindly folks seek out the dead and help them pass to their rightful rest.
moves: Reveal the terrifying nature of death
Offer information from the other side, at a price

items.name: Ghoul
items.description: Hunger. Hunger hunger hunger. Desperate clinging void-stomach-emptiness hunger. Sharp talons to rend flesh and teeth to tear and crack bones and suck out the soft marrow inside. Peasant or knight, wizard, sage, prince, or priest all make for such delicious meat.
moves: Gain the memories of their meal

items.name: Lich
items.description: At the end, they give you a scroll and a jeweled medallion to commemorate your achievements. Grand Master of Abjuration, I was called, then. It took me another ten years to learn the rituals and another four to collect the material and you see before you the fruits of my labor. I endure. I live. I will see the death of this age and the dawn of the next.
moves: Cast a perfected spell of death or destruction
Set a ritual or great working into motion
Reveal a preparation or plan already completed

items.name: Mohrg
items.description: You never get away with murder. When the gods themselves notice your misdeeds, that's where your luck runs out and a mohrg is born. The mohrg is a skeleton—flesh and skin and hair all rotted away, save their twisted, knotted guts still spilling from their bellies, magically preserved and often wrapped, noose-like, about their necks.
moves: Add to their collection of guts

items.name: Mummy
items.description: There are cultures who revere the dead, spending weeks preparing the sacred corpse for its eternal rest in temples, pyramids, and great vaults of stone populated with slaves, pets and gold. Do not be tempted by these vaults—the honored dead do not wish to be disturbed, and thievery will only raise their ire.

items.name: Nightwing
items.description: Empowered by the negative light of Death's domain, nightwings take the shape of massive, shadowy, winged creatures and travel in predatory flocks, swooping down to strip the flesh from cattle, horses and unlucky peasants out past curfew. Watch the night sky for their red eyes.

items.name: Shadow
items.description: We call to the elements. We call on fire, ever-burning. The elemental we call upon this night knows another name: the element of Night. Shadow, we name you. Death's messenger and black assassin, we claim for our own. Accept our sacrifice and do our bidding 'til the morning come.
moves: Spawn another shadow from the dead

items.name: Sigben
items.description: Sent by vampires on their two, twisted legs, these ugly things look like the head of a rat or a crocodile, furry though and sharp of tooth, with withered wings they cannot use and long, whipping tails spurred with poison tips. Stupid, vengeful and mischievous.

items.name: Skeleton
items.description: Dem bones, dem bones, dem dry bones.
items.instinct: To take the semblance of life
moves: Act out what it did in life
Snuff out the warmth of life

items.name: Spectre
items.description: For some folk, when they pass, Death himself cannot release their grip on the places they love most. They act not out of the usual hunger that drives the undead, but jealousy—jealousy that anyone else might come to love their home as much as they do and drive them out.
items.instinct: To drive life from a place
moves: Turn their haunt against a creature

items.name: Vampire
items.description: We fear them, because they call to us—so much like us, or how we hope to be: beautiful, passionate, and powerful. Every time they feed they run the risk of passing along their torture to another, and in each one lives the twisted seed of its creator. Vampires beget vampires. Suffering begets suffering.

items.name: Wight-Wolf
items.description: Like the nightwing, the wight-wolf is a creature not spawned in our world, slipping the seals of the Black Gates of Death to take the shape of massive hounds or shadowy wolves and hunt the living for sport. They travel in packs, led by a mighty alpha, bearing a kind of intelligence unknown to true canines.

items.name: Zombie
items.description: When there's no more room in Hell…
moves: Gain strength from the dead, spawn more zombies

items.name: Assassin Vine
items.description: Among the animals there exists a clear division 'tween hunter and hunted. Such a split cuts the world of leaves and flowers in twain, as well. Paths into the deep woods covered in creeping vines, and with a snap, these hungry ropes snap tight, dragging their meaty prey into the underbrush.

items.name: Blink Dog
items.description: Now you see it, now you don't. Hounds once owned by a sorcerer lord and imbued with a kind of illusory cloak, they escaped into the woods and began to breed with wolves and wild dogs. Spotted by the glittering silver of their coats and their strange, ululating howls, they have a remarkable talent for being not quite where they appear to be.
moves: Give the appearance of being somewhere they're not

items.name: Centaur
items.description: It will be a gathering of clans unseen in this age. Too long have the men cut the ancient trees for their ships. It will be a cleansing fire from the darkest woods. Raise the red banner of war! Today we strike back against these apes and retake what is ours!

items.name: Chaos Ooze
special_qualities: Fragments of other planes embedded in it
items.description: The barrier between Dungeon World and the elemental planes is not, as you might hope, a wall of stone—it's much more porous. Bits and pieces of the chaos spill out, squirming and squishing around, warping all it touches into some other, strange form. Chaos begets chaos, and it grows.
moves: Cause a change in appearance or substance

items.name: Cockatrice
items.description: A lizard of a sort, with a beak and gray feathers like a chicken. Found in a nest at the foot of a tree, quick to peck at anyone who tries to steal its eggs—and its victims freeze up all frozen, like a dog left out overnight in winter.
moves: Start a slow transformation to stone

items.name: Dryad
items.description: More beautiful by far than any man or woman born in the civil realms. To gaze upon one is to fall in love, deep and punishing. Their love is a primal thing, married to the woods—to a great oak that serves as home and mother and sacred place to them. It's a curse to see one; they'll never love you back.

items.name: Eagle Lord
items.description: Some the size of horses. Bigger, even—the kings and queens of the eagles. The ancient wizards forged a pact with them in the primordial days: men would take the plains and valleys and leave the mountaintops to the eagle lords. Lucky are the elves, for the makers of their treaties yet live.

items.name: Elvish Warrior
items.description: As with all things they undertake, the elves approach war as an art. A warrior-maiden clad in plate that shone like the winter sky, seeming to glide between the trees the way an angel might, striking out and bathing her blade in blood that steamed in the cold air.

items.name: Elvish High Arcanist
items.description: True elvish magic isn't like the spells of men. Mannish wizardry is all rotes and formulas; elvish magic requires a fine ear to hear the arcane symphony that sings in the woods and the voice with which to harmonize with what is already resounding. The High Arcanists have become more and less than any elf; the beat of their blood is the throbbing of all magic in this world.
moves: Work the magic that nature demands

items.name: Griffin
items.description: These creatures have the regal haughtiness of a lion and the arrogant bearing of an eagle, tempered with the unshakeable loyalty of both. To earn the friendship of a griffin is to have an ally all your living days. If you're ever lucky enough to meet one, be respectful and deferential above all else.

items.name: Hill Giant
items.description: Ever seen an ogre before? Bigger than that. Dumber and meaner, too. Hope you like having cows thrown at you.

items.name: Ogre
items.description: Somewhere in the not-so-long history of the mannish race there was a divide: one camp built the first city to honor the gods, the others retreated into darkness and grew tall and strong and full of hate. We have forged steel and they match it with their savagery.
items.instinct: To return the world to darker days

items.name: Razor Boar
items.description: The tusks of the razor boar shred metal plate like so much tissue. Voracious, savage and unstoppable, they tower over their mundane kin. A razor boar killed the Drunkard King in a single thrust, so they say.

items.name: Satyr
items.description: One of only a very few creatures found in the old woods that don't outright want to maim, kill, or eat us. They dwell in glades pierced by the sun, dancing on their funny goat-legs to enchanting music. They smile easily and treat our kind with friendliness, so long as you please them—but very few things hold a grudge like the stubborn satyr.
moves: Pull others into revelry through magic
Play jokes with illusions and tricks

items.name: Sprite
items.description: I'd classify them elementals, except that 'being annoying' isn't an element.
moves: Play a trick to expose someone's true nature

items.name: Treant
items.description: Old and tall and thick of bark, walk amidst the tree-lined dark. Strong and slow and forest-born, treants anger quick, we warn: if to woods with axe ye go, know the treants be thy foe.

items.name: Werewolf
items.description: Cursed, passed on by a bite to make more of their kind—the sorcerer-kings called it 'lycanthropy' in their day. There is no cure. A werewolf transforms to pass unnoticed as beast or man, hunting like both, dreading what they must ask a loved one to do to end it.
items.instinct: To shed the appearance of civilization
moves: Transform to pass unnoticed as beast or man

items.name: Worg
items.description: As horses are to the civil races, so go the worg to the goblins. Mounts, fierce in battle, ridden by only the bravest and most dangerous, are found and bred in the forest primeval to serve the goblins in their wars on men.

items.name: Athletics
items.description: General level of physical fitness — jumping, running, climbing, swimming.

stunts.name: Sprinter
stunts.effect: Move two zones for free in a conflict without rolling, instead of one, provided there are no situation aspects restricting movement.

stunts.name: Hardcore Parkour
stunts.effect: +2 to overcome actions with Athletics if you are in a chase across rooftops or a similarly precarious environment.

stunts.name: Dazing Counter
stunts.effect: When you succeed with style on a defend action against an opponent's Fight roll, you automatically counter with some sort of nerve punch or stunning blow. You get to attach the Dazed situation aspect to your opponent with a free invoke, instead of just a boost.

items.name: Burglary
items.description: Aptitude for stealing things and getting into places that are off-limits.

stunts.name: Always a Way Out
stunts.effect: +2 on Burglary rolls made to create an advantage whenever you're trying to escape from a location.

stunts.name: Security Specialist
stunts.effect: You don't have to be present to provide active opposition to someone trying to overcome security measures you put in place or worked on.

stunts.name: Talk the Talk
stunts.effect: You can use Burglary in place of Contacts whenever you're dealing specifically with other thieves and burglars.

items.name: Contacts
items.description: Knowing and making connections with people; networking.

stunts.name: Ear to the Ground
stunts.effect: Whenever someone initiates a conflict against you in an area where you've built a network of contacts, you use Contacts instead of Notice to determine turn order.

stunts.name: Rumormonger
stunts.effect: +2 to create an advantage when you plant vicious rumors about someone else.

stunts.name: The Weight of Reputation
stunts.effect: You can use Contacts instead of Provoke to create advantages based on the fear generated by the sinister reputation you've cultivated for yourself.

items.name: Crafts
items.description: Working with machinery, for good or ill.

stunts.name: Always Making Useful Things
stunts.effect: You don't ever have to spend a fate point to declare that you have the proper tools for a particular job using Crafts, even in extreme situations.

stunts.name: Better than New!
stunts.effect: Whenever you succeed with style on an overcome action to repair a piece of machinery, you can immediately give it a new situation aspect with a free invoke.

stunts.name: Surgical Strikes
stunts.effect: When using Crafts in a conflict involving machinery, you can filter out unwanted targets from whole-zone attacks without having to divide up your shifts.

items.name: Deceive
items.description: Lying to and misdirecting people.

stunts.name: Lies upon Lies
stunts.effect: +2 to create a Deceive advantage against someone who has believed one of your lies already during this session.

stunts.name: Mind Games
stunts.effect: You can use Deceive in place of Provoke to make mental attacks, as long as you can make up a clever lie as part of the attack.

stunts.name: One Person, Many Faces
stunts.effect: Whenever you meet someone new, you can spend a fate point to declare that you've met that person before under a different identity. Create a situation aspect to represent your cover story.

items.name: Drive
items.description: Operating vehicles and things that go fast.

stunts.name: Hard to Shake
stunts.effect: +2 to Drive whenever you're pursuing another vehicle in a chase scene.

stunts.name: Pedal to the Metal
stunts.effect: Whenever you're engaged in any contest where speed is the primary factor and you tie with your Drive roll, it's considered a success.

stunts.name: Ramming Speed!
stunts.effect: When ramming another vehicle, you ignore two shifts of damage.

items.name: Empathy
items.description: Knowing and being able to spot changes in a person's mood or bearing.

stunts.name: Lie Whisperer
stunts.effect: +2 to all Empathy rolls made to discern or discover lies.

stunts.name: Nose for Trouble
stunts.effect: You can use Empathy instead of Notice to determine your turn order in a conflict, provided you've observed or spoken to those involved for at least a few minutes.

items.name: Fight
items.description: All forms of close-quarters combat, both unarmed and using weapons.

stunts.name: Heavy Hitter
stunts.effect: When you succeed with style on a Fight attack and choose to reduce the result by one to gain a boost, you gain a full situation aspect with a free invocation instead.

stunts.name: Backup Weapon
stunts.effect: Whenever someone's about to hit you with a Disarmed situation aspect, spend a fate point to declare you have a backup weapon. Your opponent gets a boost instead.

items.name: Investigate
items.description: Finding things out through concentrated effort and in-depth scrutiny.

stunts.name: Attention to Detail
stunts.effect: You can use Investigate instead of Empathy to defend against Deceive attempts.

stunts.name: Eavesdropper
stunts.effect: On a successful Investigate roll to create an advantage by eavesdropping, you can discover or create one additional aspect.

items.name: Lore
items.description: Knowledge and education.

stunts.name: I've Read about That!
stunts.effect: Spend a fate point to use Lore in place of any other skill for one roll or exchange, provided you can justify having read about the action.

stunts.name: Shield of Reason
stunts.effect: You can use Lore as a defense against Provoke attempts, provided you can justify overcoming your fear through rational thought.

stunts.name: Specialist
stunts.effect: Choose a field of specialization. You get +2 to all Lore rolls relating to that field.

items.name: Notice
items.description: Situational awareness and spotting things.

stunts.name: Danger Sense
stunts.effect: Your Notice skill works unimpeded by conditions like total concealment, darkness, or other sensory impairments in situations where someone intends to harm you.

stunts.name: Body Language Reader
stunts.effect: You can use Notice in place of Empathy to learn the aspects of a target through observation.

items.name: Physique
items.description: Natural physical aptitudes — raw strength and endurance.
items.special: Average (+1) or Fair (+2) gives a 3-point stress box. Good (+3) or Great (+4) gives 3-point and 4-point stress boxes. Superb (+5)+ gives an additional mild consequence slot.

stunts.name: Grappler
stunts.effect: +2 to Physique rolls made to create advantages on an enemy by wrestling or grappling with them.

stunts.name: Take the Blow
stunts.effect: You can use Physique to defend against Fight attacks made with fists or blunt instruments, though you always take 1 shift of stress on a tie.

stunts.name: Tough as Nails
stunts.effect: Once per session, at the cost of a fate point, you can reduce the severity of a moderate physical consequence to mild, or erase a mild consequence altogether.

items.name: Provoke
items.description: Getting someone's dander up — eliciting fear, anger, shame.

stunts.name: Armor of Fear
stunts.effect: You can use Provoke to defend against Fight attacks, but only until the first time you're dealt stress in a conflict.

stunts.name: Provoke Violence
stunts.effect: When you create an advantage on an opponent using Provoke, you can use your free invocation to become the target of that character's next relevant action.

stunts.name: Okay, Fine!
stunts.effect: You can use Provoke in place of Empathy to learn a target's aspects, by bullying them until they reveal one. The target defends with Will.

items.name: Rapport
items.description: Making positive connections to people; being liked and trusted.

stunts.name: Best Foot Forward
stunts.effect: Twice per session, you may upgrade a boost you receive with Rapport into a full situation aspect with a free invocation.

stunts.name: Demagogue
stunts.effect: +2 to Rapport when you're delivering an inspiring speech in front of a crowd.

stunts.name: Popular
stunts.effect: If you're in an area where you're popular and well-liked, you can use Rapport in place of Contacts.

items.name: Resources
items.description: General level of material wealth and ability to apply it.

stunts.name: Money Talks
stunts.effect: You can use Resources instead of Rapport in any situation where ostentatious displays of material wealth might aid your cause.

stunts.name: Savvy Investor
stunts.effect: You get an additional free invoke when you create advantages with Resources that describe a monetary return on an investment from a previous session.

stunts.name: Trust Fund Baby
stunts.effect: Twice per session, you may take a boost representing a windfall or influx of cash.

items.name: Shoot
items.description: Using ranged weaponry in conflict or against non-resisting targets.

stunts.name: Called Shot
stunts.effect: During a Shoot attack, spend a fate point and declare a specific condition you want to inflict on a target. If you succeed, you place that as a situation aspect in addition to stress.

stunts.name: Quick on the Draw
stunts.effect: You can use Shoot instead of Notice to determine turn order in any physical conflict where shooting quickly would be useful.

stunts.name: Uncanny Accuracy
stunts.effect: Once per conflict, stack an additional free invoke on an advantage you've created to represent the time you take to aim or line up a shot.

items.name: Stealth
items.description: Avoiding detection, both when hiding in place and trying to move about unseen.

stunts.name: Face in the Crowd
stunts.effect: +2 to any Stealth roll to blend into a crowd.

stunts.name: Slippery Target
stunts.effect: Provided you're in darkness or shadow, you can use Stealth to defend against Shoot attacks from enemies at least one zone away.

items.name: Will
items.description: General level of mental fortitude.
items.special: Average (+1) or Fair (+2) gives a 3-point mental stress box. Good (+3) or Great (+4) gives 3-point and 4-point mental stress boxes. Superb (+5)+ gives an additional mild consequence slot for mental harm.

stunts.name: Strength From Determination
stunts.effect: Use Will instead of Physique on any overcome rolls representing feats of strength.

stunts.name: Hard Boiled
stunts.effect: You can choose to ignore a mild or moderate consequence for the duration of the scene. At the end of the scene it comes back worse.

stunts.name: Indomitable
stunts.effect: +2 to defend against Provoke attacks specifically related to intimidation and fear.

items.name: Adhere
items.effect: Object is covered in extremely sticky slime.

items.name: Animate Object
items.effect: Object obeys your commands as best it can. It can walk 15ft per round.

items.name: Anthropomorphize
items.effect: A touched animal either gains human intelligence or human appearance for L days.

items.name: Arcane Eye
items.effect: You can see through a magical floating eyeball that flies around at your command.

items.name: Astral Prison
items.effect: An object is frozen in time and space within an invulnerable crystal shell.

items.name: Attract
items.effect: L+1 objects are strongly magnetically attracted to each other if they come within 10 feet.

items.name: Auditory Illusion
items.effect: You create illusory sounds that seem to come from a direction of your choice.

items.name: Babble
items.effect: A creature must loudly and clearly repeat everything you think. It is otherwise mute.

items.name: Beast Form
items.effect: You and your possessions transform into a mundane animal.

items.name: Befuddle
items.effect: L creatures of your choice are unable to form new short-term memories for the duration of the spell.

items.name: Bend Fate
items.effect: Roll L+1 d20s. Whenever you must roll a d20 after casting the spell, you must choose and then discard one of the rolled results until they are all gone.

items.name: Bird Person
items.effect: Your arms turn into huge bird wings.

items.name: Body Swap
items.effect: You switch bodies with a creature you touch. If one body dies, the other dies as well.

items.name: Catherine
items.effect: A woman wearing a blue dress appears until end of spell. She will obey polite, safe requests.

items.name: Charm
items.effect: L creatures treat you like a friend.

items.name: Command
items.effect: A creature obeys a single, three-word command that does not harm it.

items.name: Comprehend
items.effect: You become fluent in all languages.

items.name: Control Plants
items.effect: Nearby plants and trees obey you and gain the ability to move at 5 feet per round.

items.name: Control Weather
items.effect: You may alter the type of weather at will, but you do not otherwise control it.

items.name: Counterspell
items.effect: Make an opposed Intelligence save against the Intelligence of the caster of a nearby spell. You may do this out of turn as a reaction, or against an ongoing magical effect. On a success, you may cancel the spell.

items.name: Deafen
items.effect: All nearby creatures are deafened.

items.name: Detect Magic
items.effect: You hear nearby magical auras singing. Volume and harmony signify the aura's power and refinement.

items.name: Disassemble
items.effect: Any of your body parts may be detached and reattached at will, without causing pain or damage. You can still control them.

items.name: Disguise
items.effect: You may alter the appearance of L characters at will as long as they remain humanoid. Attempts to duplicate other characters will seem uncanny.

items.name: Displace
items.effect: An object appears to be up to Lx10ft from its actual position.

items.name: Earthquake
items.effect: The ground begins shaking violently. Structures may be damaged or collapse.

items.name: Elasticity
items.effect: Your body can stretch up to Lx10ft.

items.name: Elemental Wall
items.effect: A straight wall of ice or fire Lx40ft long and 10ft high rises from the ground.

items.name: Filch
items.effect: L visible items teleport to your hands.

items.name: Fog Cloud
items.effect: Dense fog spreads out from you.

items.name: Frenzy
items.effect: L creatures erupt in a frenzy of violence.

items.name: Gate
items.effect: A portal to a random plane opens.

items.name: Gravity Shift
items.effect: You can change the direction of gravity (for yourself only) up to once per round.

items.name: Greed
items.effect: L creatures develop an overwhelming urge to possess a visible item of your choice.

items.name: Haste
items.effect: Your movement speed is tripled.

items.name: Hatred
items.effect: L creatures develop a deep hatred of another creature or group of creatures and wish to destroy it.

items.name: Hear Whispers
items.effect: You can hear faint sounds clearly.

items.name: Hover
items.effect: An object hovers, frictionless, 2ft above the ground. It can hold up to L humanoids.

items.name: Hypnotize
items.effect: A creature enters a trance and will truthfully answer L yes or no questions you ask it.

items.name: Icy Touch
items.effect: A thick ice layer spreads across a touched surface, up to Lx10ft in radius.

items.name: Illuminate
items.effect: A floating light moves as you command.

items.name: Increase Gravity
items.effect: The gravity in an area triples.

items.name: Invisible Tether
items.effect: Two objects within 10ft of each other cannot be moved more than 10ft apart.

items.name: Knock
items.effect: L nearby mundane or magical locks unlock.

items.name: Leap
items.effect: You can jump up to Lx10ft in the air.

items.name: Liquid Air
items.effect: The air around you becomes swimmable.

items.name: Magic Dampener
items.effect: All nearby magical effects have their effectiveness halved.

items.name: Manse
items.effect: A sturdy, furnished cottage appears for Lx12 hours. You can permit and forbid entry to it at will.

items.name: Marble Madness
items.effect: Your pockets are full of marbles, and will refill every round.

items.name: Masquerade
items.effect: L characters' appearances and voices become identical to a touched character.

items.name: Miniaturize
items.effect: You and L other touched creatures are reduced to the size of a mouse.

items.name: Mirror Image
items.effect: L illusory duplicates of yourself appear under your control.

items.name: Mirrorwalk
items.effect: A mirror becomes a gateway to another mirror that you looked into today.

items.name: Multiarm
items.effect: You gain L extra arms.

items.name: Night Sphere
items.effect: An Lx40ft wide sphere of darkness displaying the night sky appears.

items.name: Objectify
items.effect: You become any inanimate object between the size of a grand piano and an apple.

items.name: Ooze Form
items.effect: You become a living jelly.

items.name: Pacify
items.effect: L creatures have an aversion to violence.

items.name: Phantom Coach
items.effect: A ghostly coach appears until end of spell. It moves unnaturally fast over any terrain, including water.

items.name: Phobia
items.effect: L creatures become terrified of an object of your choice.

items.name: Pit
items.effect: A pit 10ft wide and Lx5ft deep opens in the ground.

items.name: Primeval Surge
items.effect: An object grows to the size of an elephant. If it is an animal, it is enraged.

items.name: Psychometry
items.effect: The referee answers L yes or no questions about a touched object.

items.name: Pull
items.effect: An object of any size is pulled directly towards you with the strength of L men for one round.

items.name: Push
items.effect: An object of any size is pushed directly away from you with the strength of L men for one round.

items.name: Raise Dead
items.effect: L skeletons rise from the ground to serve you. They are incredibly stupid and can only obey simple orders.

items.name: Raise Spirit
items.effect: The spirit of a dead body manifests and will answer L questions.

items.name: Read Mind
items.effect: You can hear the surface thoughts of nearby creatures.

items.name: Repel
items.effect: L+1 objects are strongly magnetically repelled from each other if they come within 10 feet.

items.name: Scry
items.effect: You can see through the eyes of a creature you touched earlier today.

items.name: Sculpt Elements
items.effect: All inanimate material behaves like clay in your hands.

items.name: Shroud
items.effect: L creatures are invisible until they move.

items.name: Shuffle
items.effect: L creatures instantly switch places. Determine where they end up randomly.

items.name: Sleep
items.effect: L creatures fall into a light sleep.

items.name: Smoke Form
items.effect: Your body becomes living smoke.

items.name: Snail Knight
items.effect: 10 minutes after casting, a knight sitting astride a giant snail rides into view. He is able to answer most questions related to quests and chivalry, and may aid you if he finds you worthy.

items.name: Sniff
items.effect: You can smell even the faintest traces of scents.

items.name: Sort
items.effect: Inanimate items sort themselves according to categories you set. The categories must be visually verifiable.

items.name: Spectacle
items.effect: A clearly unreal but impressive illusion of your choice appears, under your control. It may be up to the size of a palace and has full motion and sound.

items.name: Spellseize
items.effect: Cast this as a reaction to another spell going off to make a temporary copy of it that you can cast at any time before this spell ends.

items.name: Spider Climb
items.effect: You can climb surfaces like a spider.

items.name: Summon Cube
items.effect: Once per second, (6 times per round) you may summon or banish a 3-foot-wide cube of earth. New cubes must be affixed to the earth or to other cubes.

items.name: Swarm
items.effect: You become a swarm of crows, rats, or piranhas. You only take damage from area effects.

items.name: Telekinesis
items.effect: You may mentally move L items.

items.name: Telepathy
items.effect: L+1 creatures can hear each other's thoughts, no matter how far apart they move.

items.name: Teleport
items.effect: An object disappears and reappears on the ground in a visible, clear area up to Lx40ft away.

items.name: Thaumaturgic Anchor
items.effect: Object becomes the target of every spell cast near it.

items.name: Thicket
items.effect: A thicket of trees and dense brush up to Lx40ft wide suddenly sprouts up.

items.name: Time Jump
items.effect: An object disappears as it jumps Lx10 minutes into the future. When it returns, it appears in the unoccupied area nearest to where it left.

items.name: Summon Idol
items.effect: A carved stone statue the size of a four poster bed rises from the ground.

items.name: Time Rush
items.effect: Time in a 40ft bubble starts moving 10 times faster.

items.name: Time Slow
items.effect: Time in a 40ft bubble slows to 10%.

items.name: True Sight
items.effect: You see through all nearby illusions.

items.name: Upwell
items.effect: A spring of seawater appears.

items.name: Vision
items.effect: You completely control what a creature sees.

items.name: Visual Illusion
items.effect: A silent, immobile, illusion of your choice appears, up to the size of a bedroom.

items.name: Ward
items.effect: A silver circle 40ft across appears on the ground. Choose one thing that cannot cross it: Living creatures, dead creatures, projectiles or metal.

items.name: Web
items.effect: Your wrists can shoot thick webbing.

items.name: Wizard Mark
items.effect: Your finger can shoot a stream of ulfire-colored paint. This paint is only visible to you, and can be seen at any distance, even through solid objects.

items.name: X-Ray Vision
items.effect: You gain X-Ray vision.

items.name: Acid Splash
items.short_description: Orb deals 1d3 acid damage.
items.description: You fire a small orb of acid at the target. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack to hit your target. The orb deals 1d3 points of acid damage. This acid disappears after 1 round.

items.name: Arcane Mark

effects.Effect: one personal rune or mark, all of which must fit within 1 sq. ft.

items.short_description: Inscribes a personal rune on an object or creature (visible or invisible).
items.description:
This spell allows you to inscribe your personal rune or mark, which can consist of no more than six characters. The writing can be visible or invisible. An _arcane mark_ spell enables you to etch the rune upon any substance without harm to the material upon which it is placed. If an invisible mark is made, a _detect magic_ spell causes it to glow and be visible, though not necessarily understandable.

_See invisibility, true seeing_ , a _gem of seeing_ , or a _robe of eyes_ likewise allows the user to see an invisible _arcane mark_. A _read magic_ spell reveals the words, if any. The mark cannot be dispelled, but it can be removed by the caster or by an _erase_ spell.

If an _arcane mark_ is placed on a living being, the effect gradually fades in about a month.

_Arcane mark_ must be cast on an object prior to casting _instant summons_ on the same object (see that spell description for details).

items.name: Bleed
items.short_description: Cause a stabilized creature to resume dying.
items.description: You cause a living creature that is below 0 hit points but stabilized to resume dying. Upon casting this spell, you target a living creature that has -1 or fewer hit points. That creature begins dying, taking 1 point of damage per round. The creature can be stabilized later normally. This spell causes a creature that is dying to take 1 point of damage.

items.name: Create Water
items.short_description: Creates 2 gallons/level of pure water.
items.description:
This spell generates wholesome, drinkable water, just like clean rain water. Water can be created in an area as small as will actually contain the liquid, or in an area three times as large--possibly creating a downpour or filling many small receptacles. This water disappears after 1 day if not consumed.

_Note_ : Conjuration spells can't create substances or objects within a creature. Water weighs about 8 pounds per gallon. One cubic foot of water contains roughly 8 gallons and weighs about 60 pounds.

items.name: Dancing Lights

effects.Effect: Up to four lights, all within a 10-ft.-radius area

items.short_description: Creates torches or other lights.
items.description:
Depending on the version selected, you create up to four lights that resemble lanterns or torches (and cast that amount of light), or up to four glowing spheres of light (which look like will-o'-wisps), or one faintly glowing, vaguely humanoid shape. The _dancing lights_ must stay within a 10-foot-radius area in relation to each other but otherwise move as you desire (no concentration required): forward or back, up or down, straight or turning corners, or the like. The lights can move up to 100 feet per round. A light winks out if the distance between you and it exceeds the spell's range.

You can only have one _dancing lights_ spell active at any one time. If you cast this spell while another casting is still in effect, the previous casting is dispelled. If you make this spell permanent, it does not count against this limit.

_Dancing lights_ can be made permanent with a _permanency_ spell.

items.name: Daze

components.text: a pinch of wool or similar substance

items.component_text: V, S, M (a pinch of wool or similar substance)

effects.Target: one humanoid creature of 4 HD or less

items.short_description: A single humanoid creature with 4 HD or less loses its next action.
items.description: This spell clouds the mind of a humanoid creature with 4 or fewer Hit Dice so that it takes no actions. Humanoids of 5 or more HD are not affected. A dazed subject is not stunned, so attackers get no special advantage against it. After a creature has been dazed by this spell, it is immune to the effects of this spell for 1 minute.

items.name: Detect Magic
items.short_description: Detects all spells and magic items within 60 ft.
items.description:
You detect magical auras. The amount of information revealed depends on how long you study a particular area or subject.  
  
_1st Round_ Presence or absence of magical auras.

_2nd Round_ Number of different magical auras and the power of the most potent aura.

_3rd Round_ The strength and location of each aura. If the items or creatures bearing the auras are in line of sight, you can make Knowledge (arcana) skill checks to determine the school of magic involved in each. (Make one check per aura: DC 15 + spell level, or 15 + 1/2 caster level for a nonspell effect.) If the aura emanates from a magic item, you can attempt to identify its properties (see Spellcraft).

Magical areas, multiple types of magic, or strong local magical emanations may distort or conceal weaker auras.

_Aura Strength_ An aura's power depends on a spell's functioning spell level or an item's caster level; see the accompanying table. If an aura falls into more than one category, _detect magic_ indicates the stronger of the two.

_Lingering Aura_ A magical aura lingers after its original source dissipates (in the case of a spell) or is destroyed (in the case of a magic item). If _detect magic_ is cast and directed at such a location, the spell indicates an aura strength of dim (even weaker than a faint aura). How long the aura lingers at this dim level depends on its original power:

##### Original Strength

Original Strength| Duration of Lingering Aura  
---|---  
Faint| 1d6 rounds  
Moderate| 1d6 minutes  
Strong| 1d6 × 10 minutes  
Overwhelming| 1d6 days

##### Detect Magic

Spell or Object| Aura Power  
---|---  
Faint| Moderate| Strong| Overwhelming  
Functioning spell (spell level)| 3rd or lower| 4th-6th| 7th-9th| 10th+ (deity-level)  
Magic item (caster level)| 5th or lower| 6th-11th| 12th-20th| 21st+ (artifact)

items.name: Detect Poison

effects.Target or Area: one creature, one object, or a 5-ft. cube

items.short_description: Detects poison in a creature or object.
items.description: You determine whether a creature, object, or area has been poisoned or is poisonous. You can determine the exact type of poison with a DC 20 Wisdom check. A character with the Craft (alchemy) skill may try a DC 20 Craft (alchemy) check if the Wisdom check fails, or may try the Craft (alchemy) check prior to the Wisdom check. The spell can penetrate barriers, but 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt blocks it.

items.name: Disrupt Undead
items.short_description: Deals 1d6 damage to one undead.
items.description: You direct a ray of positive energy. You must make a ranged touch attack to hit, and if the ray hits an undead creature, it deals 1d6 points of damage to it.

items.name: Flare
items.short_description: Dazzles one creature (-1 on attack rolls).
items.description: This cantrip creates a burst of light. If you cause the light to burst in front of a single creature, that creature is dazzled for 1 minute unless it makes a successful Fortitude save. Sightless creatures, as well as creatures already dazzled, are not affected by _flare_.

items.name: Ghost Sound

components.text: a bit of wool or a small lump of wax

items.component_text: V, S, M (a bit of wool or a small lump of wax)
items.short_description: Figment sounds.
items.description:
_Ghost sound_ allows you to create a volume of sound that rises, recedes, approaches, or remains at a fixed place. You choose what type of sound _ghost sound_ creates when casting it and cannot thereafter change the sound's basic character.

The volume of sound created depends on your level. You can produce as much noise as four normal humans per caster level (maximum 40 humans). Thus, talking, singing, shouting, walking, marching, or running sounds can be created. The noise a _ghost sound_ spell produces can be virtually any type of sound within the volume limit. A horde of rats running and squeaking is about the same volume as eight humans running and shouting. A roaring lion is equal to the noise from 16 humans, while a roaring dragon is equal to the noise from 32 humans. Anyone who hears a _ghost sound_ receives a Will save to disbelieve.

_Ghost sound_ can enhance the effectiveness of a _silent image_ spell.

_Ghost sound_ can be made permanent with a _permanency_ spell.

items.name: Guidance
items.short_description: +1 on one attack roll, saving throw, or skill check.
items.description: This spell imbues the subject with a touch of divine guidance. The creature gets a +1 competence bonus on a single attack roll, saving throw, or skill check. It must choose to use the bonus before making the roll to which it applies.

items.name: Know Direction
items.short_description: You discern north.
items.description: When you cast this spell, you instantly know the direction of north from your current position. The spell is effective in any environment in which "north" exists, but it may not work in extraplanar settings. Your knowledge of north is correct at the moment of casting, but you can get lost again within moments if you don't find some external reference point to help you keep track of direction.

items.name: Light

components.text: a firefly
a firefly

items.short_description: Object shines like a torch.
items.description:
This spell causes a touched object to glow like a torch, shedding normal light in a 20-foot radius from the point touched, and increasing the light level for an additional 20 feet by one step, up to normal light (darkness becomes dim light, and dim light becomes normal light). In an area of normal or bright light, this spell has no effect. The effect is immobile, but it can be cast on a movable object.

You can only have one _light_ spell active at any one time. If you cast this spell while another casting is still in effect, the previous casting is dispelled. If you make this spell permanent (through _permanency_ or a similar effect), it does not count against this limit. _Light_ can be used to counter or dispel any darkness spell of equal or lower spell level.

items.name: Lullaby
items.short_description: Makes subject drowsy: -5 on Perception checks, -2 on Will saves against sleep.
items.description: Any creature within the area that fails a Will save becomes drowsy and inattentive, taking a -5 penalty on Perception checks and a -2 penalty on Will saves against _sleep_ effects while the _lullaby_ is in effect. _Lullaby_ lasts for as long as the caster concentrates, plus up to 1 round per caster level thereafter.

items.name: Mage Hand

effects.Target: one nonmagical, unattended object weighing up to 5 lbs.

items.short_description: 5-pound telekinesis.
items.description: You point your finger at an object and can lift it and move it at will from a distance. As a move action, you can propel the object as far as 15 feet in any direction, though the spell ends if the distance between you and the object ever exceeds the spell's range.

items.name: Mending

effects.Target: one object of up to 1 lb./level

items.short_description: Makes minor repairs on an object.
items.description: This spell repairs damaged objects, restoring 1d4 hit points to the object. If the object has the broken condition, this condition is removed if the object is restored to at least half its original hit points. All of the pieces of an object must be present for this spell to function. Magic items can be repaired by this spell, but you must have a caster level equal to or higher than that of the object. Magic items that are destroyed (at 0 hit points or less) can be repaired with this spell, but this spell does not restore their magic abilities. This spell does not affect creatures (including constructs). This spell has no effect on objects that have been warped or otherwise transmuted, but it can still repair damage done to such items.

items.name: Message

components.text: a piece of copper wire

items.component_text: V, S, F (a piece of copper wire)

effects.Targets: one creature/level

items.short_description: Whisper conversation at distance.
items.description: You can whisper messages and receive whispered replies. Those nearby can hear these messages with a DC 25 Perception check. You point your finger at each creature you want to receive the message. When you whisper, the whispered message is audible to all targeted creatures within range. Magical _silence_ , 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal (or a thin sheet of lead), or 3 feet of wood or dirt blocks the spell. The message does not have to travel in a straight line. It can circumvent a barrier if there is an open path between you and the subject, and the path's entire length lies within the spell's range. The creatures that receive the message can whisper a reply that you hear. The spell transmits sound, not meaning; it doesn't transcend language barriers. To speak a message, you must mouth the words and whisper.

items.name: Open/Close

components.text: a brass key

effects.Target: object weighing up to 30 lbs. or portal that can be opened or closed

items.short_description: Opens or closes small or light things.
items.description: You can open or close (your choice) a door, chest, box, window, bag, pouch, bottle, barrel, or other container. If anything resists this activity (such as a bar on a door or a lock on a chest), the spell fails. In addition, the spell can only open and close things weighing 30 pounds or less. Thus, doors, chests, and similar objects sized for enormous creatures may be beyond this spell's ability to affect.

items.name: Prestidigitation
items.short_description: Performs minor tricks.
items.description: Prestidigitations are minor tricks that novice spellcasters use for practice. Once cast, a _prestidigitation_ spell enables you to perform simple magical effects for 1 hour. The effects are minor and have severe limitations. A prestidigitation can slowly lift 1 pound of material. It can color, clean, or soil items in a 1-foot cube each round. It can chill, warm, or flavor 1 pound of nonliving material. It cannot deal damage or affect the concentration of spellcasters. _Prestidigitation_ can create small objects, but they look crude and artificial. The materials created by a _prestidigitation_ spell are extremely fragile, and they cannot be used as tools, weapons, or spell components. Finally, _prestidigitation_ lacks the power to duplicate any other spell effects. Any actual change to an object (beyond just moving, cleaning, or soiling it) persists only 1 hour.

items.name: Purify Food And Drink

effects.Target: 1 cu. ft./level of contaminated food and water

items.short_description: Purifies 1 cu. ft./level of food or water.
items.description: This spell makes spoiled, rotten, diseased, poisonous, or otherwise contaminated food and water pure and suitable for eating and drinking. This spell does not prevent subsequent natural decay or spoilage. Unholy water and similar food and drink of significance is spoiled by _purify food and drink_ , but the spell has no effect on creatures of any type nor upon magic potions. Water weighs about 8 pounds per gallon. One cubic foot of water contains roughly 8 gallons and weighs about 60 pounds.

items.name: Ray Of Frost
items.short_description: Ray deals 1d3 cold damage.
items.description: A ray of freezing air and ice projects from your pointing finger. You must succeed on a ranged touch attack with the ray to deal damage to a target. The ray deals 1d3 points of cold damage.

items.name: Read Magic

components.text: a clear crystal or mineral prism

items.component_text: V, S, F (a clear crystal or mineral prism)
items.short_description: Read scrolls and spellbooks.
items.description:
You can decipher magical inscriptions on objects--books, scrolls, weapons, and the like--that would otherwise be unintelligible. This deciphering does not normally invoke the magic contained in the writing, although it may do so in the case of a cursed or trapped scroll. Furthermore, once the spell is cast and you have read the magical inscription, you are thereafter able to read that particular writing without recourse to the use of _read magic_. You can read at the rate of one page (250 words) per minute. The spell allows you to identify a _glyph of warding_ with a DC 13 Spellcraft check, a _greater glyph of warding_ with a DC 16 Spellcraft check, or any _symbol_ spell with a Spellcraft check (DC 10 + spell level).

_Read magic_ can be made permanent with a _permanency_ spell.

items.name: Resistance

components.text: a miniature cloak
a miniature cloak

items.short_description: Subject gains +1 on saving throws.
items.description:
You imbue the subject with magical energy that protects it from harm, granting it a +1 resistance bonus on saves.

_Resistance_ can be made permanent with a _permanency_ spell.

items.name: Stabilize
items.short_description: Cause a dying creature to stabilize.
items.description: Upon casting this spell, you target a living creature that has -1 or fewer hit points. That creature is automatically stabilized and does not lose any further hit points. If the creature later takes damage, it continues dying normally.

items.name: Summon Instrument
items.short_description: Summons one musical instrument.
items.description: This spell summons one handheld musical instrument of your choice. This instrument appears in your hands or at your feet (your choice). The instrument is typical for its type. Only one instrument appears per casting, and it will play only for you. You can't summon an instrument too large to be held in two hands. The summoned instrument disappears at the end of this spell.

items.name: Touch Of Fatigue

components.text: a drop of sweat

items.component_text: V, S, M (a drop of sweat)
items.short_description: Touch attack fatigues target.
items.description:
You channel negative energy through your touch, fatiguing the target. You must succeed on a touch attack to strike a target. The subject is immediately fatigued for the spell's duration.

This spell has no effect on a creature that is already fatigued. Unlike with normal fatigue, the effect ends as soon as the spell's duration expires.

items.name: Virtue
items.short_description: Subject gains 1 temporary hp.
items.description: With a touch, you infuse a creature with a tiny surge of life, granting the subject 1 temporary hit point.

items.name: Alarm

components.text: a tiny bell and a piece of very fine silver wire
a tiny bell and a piece of very fine silver wire

items.component_text: V, S, F/DF (a tiny bell and a piece of very fine silver wire)

effects.Area: 20-ft.-radius emanation centered on a point in space

items.short_description: Wards an area for 2 hours/level.
items.description:
A _larm_ creates a subtle ward on an area you select. Once the spell effect is in place, it thereafter sounds a mental or audible alarm each time a creature of Tiny or larger size enters the warded area or touches it. A creature that speaks the password (determined by you at the time of casting) does not set off the _alarm_. You decide at the time of casting whether the _alarm_ will be mental or audible in nature.

_Mental Alarm_ : A mental _alarm_ alerts you (and only you) so long as you remain within 1 mile of the warded area. You note a single mental "ping" that awakens you from normal sleep but does not otherwise disturb concentration. A _silence_ spell has no effect on a mental _alarm_.

_Audible Alarm_ : An audible _alarm_ produces the sound of a hand bell, and anyone within 60 feet of the warded area can hear it clearly. Reduce the distance by 10 feet for each interposing closed door and by 20 feet for each substantial interposing wall.

In quiet conditions, the ringing can be heard faintly as far as 180 feet away. The sound lasts for 1 round. Creatures within a _silence_ spell cannot hear the ringing. 

Ethereal or astral creatures do not trigger the _alarm_.

_Alarm_ can be made permanent with a _permanency_ spell.

items.name: Animal Messenger

components.text: a morsel of food the animal likes

items.component_text: V, S, M (a morsel of food the animal likes)
items.short_description: Sends a Tiny animal to a specific place.
items.description:
You compel a Tiny animal to go to a spot you designate. The most common use for this spell is to get an animal to carry a message to your allies. The animal cannot be one tamed or trained by someone else, including such creatures as familiars and animal companions.

Using some type of food desirable to the animal as a lure, you call the animal to you. It advances and awaits your bidding. You can mentally impress on the animal a certain place well known to you or an obvious landmark. The directions must be simple, because the animal depends on your knowledge and can't find a destination on its own. You can attach a small item or note to the messenger. The animal then goes to the designated location and waits there until the duration of the spell expires, whereupon it resumes its normal activities.

During this period of waiting, the messenger allows others to approach it and remove any scroll or token it carries. The intended recipient gains no special ability to communicate with the animal or read any attached message (if it's written in a language he doesn't know, for example).

items.name: Animate Rope

effects.Target: one rope-like object, length up to 50 ft. + 5 ft./level; see text

items.short_description: Makes a rope move at your command.
items.description:
You can animate a nonliving rope-like object. The maximum length assumes a rope with a 1-inch diameter. Reduce the maximum length by 50% for every additional inch of thickness, and increase it by 50% for each reduction of the rope's diameter by half.

The possible commands are "coil" (form a neat, coiled stack), "coil and knot," "loop," "loop and knot," "tie and knot," and the opposites of all of the above ("uncoil," and so forth). You can give one command each round as a move action, as if directing an active spell.

The rope can enwrap only a creature or an object within 1 foot of it--it does not snake outward--so it must be thrown near the intended target. Doing so requires a successful ranged touch attack roll (range increment 10 feet). A typical 1-inch-diameter hemp rope has 2 hit points, AC 10, and requires a DC 23 Strength check to burst it. The rope does not deal damage, but it can be used as a trip line or to cause a single opponent that fails a Reflex saving throw to become entangled. A creature capable of spellcasting that is bound by this spell must make a concentration check with a DC of 15 + the spell's level to cast a spell. An entangled creature can slip free with a DC 20 Escape Artist check.

The rope itself and any knots tied in it are not magical.

The spell cannot affect objects carried or worn by a creature.

items.name: Bane
items.short_description: Enemies take -1 on attack rolls and saves vs. fear.
items.description: _Bane_ fills your enemies with fear and doubt. Each affected creature takes a -1 penalty on attack rolls and a -1 penalty on saving throws against fear effects. _Bane_ counters and dispels _bless_.

items.name: Bless

effects.Area: The caster and all allies within a 50-ft. burst, centered on the caster

items.short_description: Allies gain +1 on attack rolls and saves against fear.
items.description:
_Bless_ fills your allies with courage. Each ally gains a +1 morale bonus on attack rolls and on saving throws against fear effects.

_Bless_ counters and dispels _bane_.

items.name: Bless Water

components.text: 5 pounds of powdered silver worth 25 gp

items.component_text: V, S, M (5 pounds of powdered silver worth 25 gp)
items.short_description: Makes holy water.
items.description: This transmutation imbues a flask (1 pint) of water with positive energy, turning it into holy water.

items.name: Bless Weapon
items.short_description: Weapon strikes true against evil foes.
items.description:
This transmutation makes a weapon strike true against evil foes. The weapon is treated as having a +1 enhancement bonus for the purpose of bypassing the DR of evil creatures or striking evil incorporeal creatures (though the spell doesn't grant an actual enhancement bonus). The weapon also becomes good-aligned, which means it can bypass the DR of certain creatures. (This effect overrides and suppresses any other alignment the weapon might have.) Individual arrows or bolts can be transmuted, but affected projectile weapons (such as bows) don't confer the benefit to the projectiles they shoot.

In addition, all critical hit rolls against evil foes are automatically successful, so every threat is a critical hit. This last effect does not apply to any weapon that already has a magical effect related to critical hits, such as a _keen_ weapon or a _vorpal sword_.

items.name: Burning Hands
items.short_description: 1d4/level fire damage (max 5d4).
items.description: A cone of searing flame shoots from your fingertips. Any creature in the area of the flames takes 1d4 points of fire damage per caster level (maximum 5d4). Flammable materials burn if the flames touch them. A character can extinguish burning items as a full-round action.

items.name: Calm Animals

effects.Targets: animals within 30 ft. of each other

items.short_description: Calms 2d4 + level HD of animals.
items.description:
This spell soothes and quiets animals, rendering them docile and harmless. Only ordinary animals (those with Intelligence scores of 1 or 2) can be affected by this spell. All the subjects must be of the same kind, and no two may be more than 30 feet apart. The maximum number of HD of animals you can affect is equal to 2d4 + caster level. 

The affected creatures remain where they are and do not attack or flee. They are not helpless and defend themselves normally if attacked. Any threat breaks the spell on the threatened creatures.

items.name: Cause Fear

effects.Target: one living creature with 5 or fewer HD

items.short_description: A creature of 5 HD or less flees for 1d4 rounds.
items.description: The affected creature becomes frightened. If the subject succeeds on a Will save, it is shaken for 1 round. Creatures with 6 or more HD are immune to this effect. _Cause fear_ counters and dispels _remove fear_.

items.name: Charm Animal
items.short_description: Makes one animal your friend.
items.description: This spell functions like _charm person_ , except that it affects a creature of the animal type.

items.name: Charm Person
items.short_description: Makes one person your friend.
items.description:
This charm makes a humanoid creature regard you as its trusted friend and ally (treat the target's attitude as friendly). If the creature is currently being threatened or attacked by you or your allies, however, it receives a +5 bonus on its saving throw.

The spell does not enable you to control the charmed person as if it were an automaton, but it perceives your words and actions in the most favorable way. You can try to give the subject orders, but you must win an opposed Charisma check to convince it to do anything it wouldn't ordinarily do. (Retries are not allowed.) An affected creature never obeys suicidal or obviously harmful orders, but it might be convinced that something very dangerous is worth doing. Any act by you or your apparent allies that threatens the charmed person breaks the spell. You must speak the person's language to communicate your commands, or else be good at pantomiming.

items.name: Chill Touch

effects.Targets: creature or creatures touched (up to one/level)

items.saving_throw: Fortitude partial or Will negates; see text
items.short_description: One touch/level deals 1d6 damage and possibly 1 Str damage.
items.description:
A touch from your hand, which glows with blue energy, disrupts the life force of living creatures. Each touch channels negative energy that deals 1d6 points of damage. The touched creature also takes 1 point of Strength damage unless it makes a successful Fortitude saving throw. You can use this melee touch attack up to one time per level.

An undead creature you touch takes no damage of either sort, but it must make a successful Will saving throw or flee as if panicked for 1d4 rounds + 1 round per caster level.

items.name: Color Spray

components.text: red, yellow, and blue powder or colored sand

items.component_text: V, S, M (red, yellow, and blue powder or colored sand)
items.short_description: Knocks unconscious, blinds, and/or stuns weak creatures.
items.description:
A vivid cone of clashing colors springs forth from your hand, causing creatures to become stunned, perhaps also blinded, and possibly knocking them unconscious. Each creature within the cone is affected according to its HD.

_2 HD or less_ : The creature is unconscious, blinded, and stunned for 2d4 rounds, then blinded and stunned for 1d4 rounds, and then stunned for 1 round. (Only living creatures are knocked unconscious.)

_3 or 4 HD_ The creature is blinded and stunned for 1d4 rounds, then stunned for 1 round.

_5 or more HD_ The creature is stunned for 1 round.
